name: Halftone screen
one_line: Tone rendered as a grid of dots whose size carries the value, as in offset or screen printing
summary: Continuous tone becomes a regular screen of dots, lines or squares that swell in shadows and shrink in highlights. It reads as printed matter: newsprint, comics, gig posters. Dot shape, screen angle and how the screen is locked to the frame or the subject decide whether it feels like cheap print, pop art or footage seen through a mesh.

routes.one_line: Compute the screen per pixel in a fragment shader over the source image or scene

steps.does: Turn source luminance into dot coverage per screen cell, as a function of pixel position and t

limits: No fixture renders a halftone; the screen function is yours to write and verify
WebGL evidence is a software-rendered triangle read back, not a full-frame image effect

routes.one_line: Sample the source on a grid and draw one dot per cell on a 2D canvas

steps.does: Read a tone value per cell and draw a dot scaled to it, redrawn from t on each seek

limits: Canvas 2D evidence excludes images and pixel access, which sampling a photograph needs
One dot per draw call gets slow as cells shrink

routes.one_line: Screen stills or a frame sequence from the command line before they enter the scene

steps.does: Apply a halftone threshold screen to each still or frame

limits: ImageMagick evidence covers drawing solid frames, not threshold screens
A screen baked into frames is frame-locked; it cannot ride with a moving object
